correctness.rationale: All 24 vertices and 48 graph edges are specified algebraically. The standard-library verifier rebuilds the shortest-path matrix and all 638 graph-square cliques, checks 252 distinct sequential free-face pairs of consecutive dimensions with unique cofaces, and confirms the exact remainder is a 24-vertex triangulation with 66 edges, 44 triangles, connected cyclic vertex links, and Euler characteristic 2. Thus the remainder is a 2-sphere. Scale-one clique triangles are eight vertex-disjoint triangles, removable to a graph with first Betti number 17. The proof is exhaustive for this finite graph, not an extrapolation from samples; no claims for scale three or other graphs.

originality.rationale: Comparisons were by object, metric, threshold, homotopy conclusion and implication. Full primary text covers only Platonic 1-skeletons and explicitly proposes Archimedean generalizations. Closest published Euclidean cuboctahedron has 12 vertices; graph-metric truncated tetrahedron and truncated cube are different 1-skeletons. Targeted published-finding corpus and web queries for the 24-vertex rhombicuboctahedral graph-square Rips collapse found no equivalent theorem. Indexed search is not a guarantee of novelty, and specific residual literature risks are recorded. General graph-square stability and universality theorems in Adamaszek (arXiv:1104.0433) were inspected; their hypotheses/results do not imply this fixed-graph collapse.
residual_risks: An unindexed paper, thesis, unpublished proof, or differently phrased general graph-power collapse theorem may provide implicit equivalent or stronger coverage.

value.rationale: The rhombicuboctahedron is a natural 24-vertex Archimedean solid specifically within the published question of extending polyhedral Rips calculations beyond Platonic solids. A graph-square flag complex of dimension four collapses to the actual embedded boundary 2-sphere via 252 explicit elementary steps, which is stronger than a Betti computation and makes the simple-homotopy mechanism reproducible. Its scale-one 17-cycle topology and scale-two 2-dimensional fundamental class exhibit a substantive finite metric-space topology transition, not an arbitrary minor slice.
